text.p: Manitowoc Co Inc said Thursday its board voted to discontinue the company's stock repurchase program, effective immediately, in order to conserve cash to make acquisitions.
"We would like to position ourselves to make another acquisition should we find the right fit," said president Fred Butler. "Using cash to buy our shares would be counterproductive to this strategy."

Among other factors, Butler said such repurchases would reduce available cash that could help finance an acquisition or negatively affect favorable accounting treatments that could be used in such situations.

Manitowoc, a manufacturer of ice-cube machines and commercial refrigeration equipment, said it repurchased a total of 4.0 million of its common shares, as adjusted for a three-for-two stock split on July 2, 1996, at a total investment of $71.7 million.
The last material repurchase was completed during June 1995.
